newsitem.title: UK: BT won't talk about MCI as lifts Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: BT won't talk about MCI as lifts Q1 profits.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Thursday posted a 1.4 percent rise in first quarter pre-tax profits despite rising competition but declined to comment on the future of its $20 billion merger with America's MCI Communications Corp.

BT, which along with MCI has launched a thorough review of the U.S. group's businesses after the U.S. long-distance carrier issued a surprise profit warning about three weeks ago, said increased expenditure by associate companies had held back profits.
The British telecoms giant said pre-tax profits in the first three months to June 30 rose to 881 million pounds ($1.4 billion) from 869 million on 4.3 percent higher turnover of 3.8 billion pounds.

"BT continues to deliver sound results despite having made over 200 million pounds worth of price reductions in the quarter, more than half of which related to international calls," said BT's chairman Sir Iain Vallance in the results statement.
"Demand for inland calls is healthy and there is strong growth in our newer services."
Amid rising competition, turnover from inland telephone calls was virtually static at 1.23 billion pounds with volume growth being offset almost entirely by price cuts.
Both inland and international call volume growth over a 12 month period rose to eight percent from around seven percent, BT said. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
